task_title: Supervisor panes never wake for ordinary traffic: cas-dab2 gate denies every non-lifecycle row, so worker plans/merge requests/dispatch handoffs are delivered but invisible until the supervisor polls
close_reason:
Supervisor pane wakes are now decided from the sender CAS recorded at enqueue time, and a registered worker's merge request wakes an idle supervisor without a poll.

Delivered on factory/bold-heron-25 tip a3e81f6d, merged to epic/epic-v3-15-5-coordination-follow-ups-duplicate-mes-cas-55aa at c01ce1fa. Four commits: ee4d0dd2 (cherry-pick of true-panther-6's 7f178c0c — verified identical by patch-id, so that branch retires with nothing lost), 07f6361f, ffbc7080, fda51375. Each commit green and each leaves wakes functional; the schema/population half landed before the gate half deliberately, because NULL never wakes and a gate-first landing would have silently killed every wake CAS has today.

WHAT WAS WRONG
1. The reported bug: every non-lifecycle supervisor-addressed row was inbox-only, so the messages whose purpose is to unblock the supervisor waited for a poll (merge request 24346 parked a task in AwaitingMerge; dispatch handoff 24370 blocked a close; an execution plan sat unread while the supervisor sent a status check asking why no plan had arrived).
2. The cas-15f2 bypass, folded in by supervisor ruling 24559: the peer-supervisor allowance sat IN FRONT of cas-3dcb's envelope check and turned on names_a_registered_supervisor(agents, source) — a roster lookup of a caller-settable name. `cas factory message --from "<a real supervisor's name>"` therefore skipped envelope corroboration entirely and obtained a PTY write with arbitrary text. The old unit test modelled the forgery as "the roster said no" and could not see it.

WHAT LANDED
- prompt_queue.origin_agent_id / origin_kind: additive, nullable, written ONLY by CAS's own enqueue path from an already-authenticated caller. QueueOrigin {RegisteredAgent{agent_id}, Daemon, Unattributed}; the agent id is the registry id, not a display name, so role resolution cannot be spoofed by naming someone. No backfill — inventing provenance for rows whose sender was never recorded is the fiction the columns exist to prevent.
- Stamped: MCP coordination message/interrupt and factory clear_context -> RegisteredAgent, taken from the session's registry row and never from display_name, row_source, or get_agent_id()'s literal "unknown" fallback; 11 daemon relay sites -> Daemon. `cas factory message` and bridge POST /message cannot stamp AT ALL — they reach the store through methods that take no origin parameter, so there is no expression in those routes that can produce one. That is enforcement by type system, not a runtime default. Commander/hub is left unstamped deliberately: it has a real authenticated principal, but a device credential is not a registry id and minting one would be the same fiction.
- Gate re-keyed: supervisor_wake_class(sender, supervisor_name, source, prompt). Daemon + a lifecycle/worker-died/spawn/CI/attention envelope; Registered{Supervisor} + not this pane's own echo; Registered{Worker} + a CAS-attached <cas-merge-request>. Unstamped, Unattributed and Unresolvable never wake, whatever the payload says.
- message_status separates wake_not_applicable from wake_declined_by_policy with the reason. One prefix used to cover both a routine chat row and an eligible unblock request the pane refused — opposite facts, and the second hid in a wall of the first.
- Fail-safe: one Daemon-stamped <worker-attention kind="supervisor_unread"> per distinct backlog head, naming the unread count and the oldest sender, emitted from the delivery-stalled scan that previously bounced only to senders. This is how a blocker and a verification handoff reach an idle supervisor, satisfying the acceptance criteria's "or is surfaced by an equivalent unread mechanism" clause.
- Two doc comments corrected where they asserted a property that does not hold (factory_supervisor_overlap::names_a_registered_supervisor, and the gate's copy of the same claim). Both are now marked NOT AN AUTHENTICATION CHECK and retained as display/consistency only.

EVERY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS MET
- "A merge request … sent by a registered worker to its supervisor wakes the supervisor pane": met by the Registered{Worker} + <cas-merge-request> class.
- "verification handoff, or blocker … or is surfaced by an equivalent unread mechanism": met by the supervisor_unread backlog relay.
- "a message whose `source` string is caller-set and whose sender is not a registered agent still cannot obtain a PTY write": met, and enforced by the type system at the enqueue side as well as by the gate refusing Unstamped/Unattributed/Unresolvable.
- "message_status distinguishes 'wake not applicable' from 'wake declined by policy' with the reason": met by WakeOutcome, persisted as "wake_not_applicable: <reason>" / "wake_declined_by_policy: <reason>".
- "Duplicate delivery is either fixed or explained with the two writers named": explained and fixed. cas-cdf9 measured ONE writer performing two writes — delivery.rs:855 deliver_to_worker (the teams-inbox write, which Claude Code renders as <teammate-message>) and delivery.rs:876 pty_nudge (the same text typed into the pane, appearing as the bare "CAS provenance:" turn). director_events and surface_unseen_for_recipient are both exonerated by receipt evidence. Fixed at b3d834bb, already in this branch's base. I confirmed the two call sites exist as described; I did not re-derive the store measurements.

THE THREE JUDGEMENT CALLS, all ruled ACCEPTED AS DELIVERED by the supervisor (msg 24587)
1. `source` is still READ, but only for the Daemon class, where CAS wrote both the stamp and the source. Caught against an existing test: a Closed-transition lifecycle row carries a real envelope but no `lifecycle-wake:` prefix, so envelope-only would have started waking supervisors for progress FYIs — the exact cas-dab2 noise. It is authority nowhere.
2. Only the CAS-framed merge request wakes. Blockers and verification handoffs are free text, and waking on them means waking on a keyword — the check class this task removed. They are delivered through the unread-backlog relay above. The supervisor took the separate follow-up for CAS-emitted blocker/verification-dispatch envelopes as his own and instructed me not to open it; that is a future enhancement, not residual work from this task.
3. The peer-supervisor class trusts the stamped registry Supervisor role with no envelope requirement, stated out loud in the code rather than left implicit. There is no supervisor-to-supervisor envelope to corroborate against, and requiring one would kill the wake v3.15.4 just shipped.

Also load-bearing, and easy to misread as tidiness: wake-eligible rows are excluded from the unread count, because the summary is itself a lifecycle-wake row and would otherwise become its own backlog head without end. And `supervisor_unread` is registered in BOTH worker-attention parsers — the wake-corroboration check and message_ack's outbox-key bridge — since missing the second acks the durable notification and leaves the prompt relay visible in every later worker_status.

worktree_merge no longer reports an unpublished target as diverged, and no longer hands the operator a recovery that cannot work. Root cause was cas-cli/src/worktree/git/branch_ops.rs returning TargetReconcile::Diverged on ahead>0 alone, so a target with ahead=N/behind=0 was classified as divergence and the caller printed "origin/<target> is at X with 0 commit(s) you do not have" plus a `git merge origin/<target>` recipe that is a no-op in that state — the measured loop where following the instruction produced the identical refusal.

FIX (c977e9b9): divergence now requires ahead>0 AND behind>0; the remaining state has its own TargetReconcile::AheadOfRemote { local, remote, ahead }. describe_target_reconcile gained an arm that states the unpublished count and both tips, says plainly it is not a divergence, and points at the branch's normal publication path, never the fetch/merge/retry recipe and never a force-push. Ahead-only proceeds to merge, a design choice recorded before coding and accepted by the supervisor: with behind=0 origin has not advanced, so a later push fast-forwards and there is nothing to reconcile. Protected-branch policy is unchanged — PROTECTED_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REQUIRES_PR, dirty-tree protections and task target authority are untouched, and no direct-main push was made.

- Contention, three layers: the vector-queue writes (`retire`, `sync_file_symbols`, schema DDL on open) take the write lock up front with bounded retry; the code-store writes on the retire/publish path (`add_file`, `add_symbol`, `delete_symbol`, `delete_symbols_in_file`, `delete_file`) go through `shared_db::with_write_retry`, and the two batch writers through `with_immediate_write_txn`; the BM25 publish waits out a writer lock held by a concurrent `cas serve` with one WriterLockBudget shared across the run (per-file retries would have multiplied across 592 files).

Root cause, verified at file:line rather than assumed: crates/cas-mcp-proxy/src/config.rs:328 `merged.allowlist = project.allowlist` — a project proxy file REPLACES the machine allowlist rather than widening it — combined with `run()` only ever loading and saving `paths.user_proxy`. - `run()` takes `project_proxy: Option<&Path>`; `execute()` resolves it via the same `find_cas_root` ancestor walk the proxy loader uses, so the command repairs the very file doctor reads.
- The file is edited with `toml_edit`, not round-tripped through `ProxyConfig`: comments, key order, multi-line array shape and every unrelated server and route survive byte-for-byte.
- Its mecha-cassy routes are rewritten to MECHA_CASSY_TOOLS. Its `[servers.mecha-cassy]` block is removed only when it parses equal to the machine registration this run wrote or found current; a block that differs is an override, such as a project aimed at a staging hub, and is kept and named, because dropping it would silently move that project to another endpoint. Keeping is not a change, so a run over an override stays idempotent.
- `report.allowlist` is now the effective policy, so drift is measured against what will actually dispatch, and "already-configured" cannot be printed while a shadowing file drifts.
- A project file that names no hub route is left untouched and reported with the exact routes to add, rather than offered a re-run that cannot work.
- `ToolDrift::describe` takes the source path, so the doctor drift row names the file the stale entries live in.

Merged into epic/epic-cas-doctor-warnings-the-operator-cannot-clear-cas-8094 as df0e8550 (factory/agile-crane-5 @ aa384a61; 2f11e28e tests-first, aa384a61 implementation). (1) Registry writes skip disposable roots. `store/known_repos.rs` gains `RegistrySkip{Artifacts,Scratch,Temp}` + `registry_skip()`; `register_repo`, `register_repo_strict` and `worktree::discovery::seed` all consult it and log the reason at debug. A skip returns Ok, not Err, so the boot paths that `?` the strict call keep booting. Artifacts roots resolve from three sources — the default host artifacts directory, the candidate's own `.cas/config.toml` (an artifacts copy carries the config it was copied from), and the ambient project store — so a configured `[factory] artifacts_root` is honoured. The temp rule is narrow on purpose: only a directory directly under the system temp directory carrying a `temp_hygiene::TEMP_ROOT_PREFIXES` name. A blanket system-temp rule was tried and rejected, because every TestEnvGuard fixture HOME is itself a system-temp directory; that rule would have silently disabled registration across the suite and for any operator whose checkout lives on a temp mount.

(2) Peer enumeration separates "not a project store" from "unreadable". `read_snapshot` split into `open_read_only` + `snapshot_from_conn`; new `read_peer_snapshot` returns `Ok(None)` when the peer DB has no `tasks` table. New `SkippedPeer` / `ForeignRowReport::peers_skipped` / `NOT_A_PROJECT_STORE`; `summary()` wraps `comparison_summary()` so the skipped clause appears on every branch, including the zero-peer branch where a host whose only other row is a scratch copy would otherwise read "0 project DB(s) compared" with no explanation. `peers_skipped` is deliberately absent from the doctor status expression (doctor.rs:1663) so it can never drive WARN. Genuine read failures stay loud in `peers_unreadable`, and the local DB still fails hard if it has no `tasks` table.

(3) `cas known-repos forget <path>` removes a live registry row plus any binding whose repo_root canonicalizes to the target, prints a receipt, is idempotent, and refuses the current project root without `--yes`. Bindings are removed here unlike `prune-missing`, which preserves them on purpose — forget is an explicit operator instruction about that exact repository, so a selector left aimed at it would resolve to a root the registry no longer knows. Also: `SeedReport.skipped_disposable` printed by `cas known-repos seed`, muted skipped-root lines in `cas doctor --foreign-rows`, and the new verb documented in all three supervisor `preflight.md` flavours.

task_title: Canonical worker merge leaves another linked epic checkout stale
close_reason:
A canonical worker merge no longer strands another linked checkout of the target branch.

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced before implementing and corrected from my own earlier lead: not branch_is_checked_out_here, but GitOperations::merge_branch_via_temp_worktree (cas-cli/src/worktree/git.rs). It merges in an ephemeral detached worktree and advances the branch with compare_and_swap_ref, i.e. update-ref. Git refuses `checkout` of one branch in two worktrees, but update-ref bypasses that protection and notifies nobody, so a second linked worktree keeps its old index and working tree while the ref moves. A fixture builds that exact shape in a temporary repository and, before the fix, failed with `D  delivered.txt` — the sibling reporting the merged content as a staged deletion, the same phantom reverse diff the epic integration checkout showed.

DELIVERED BEHAVIOUR, every branch decided before anything is written:
- The inventory of checkouts holding the target is read repo-wide from `git worktree list --porcelain`. If git cannot answer, the merge refuses with CheckoutInventoryUnavailable before the temp worktree, the merge and the compare-and-swap — an unknown inventory never authorizes an advance.
- A holder with uncommitted work refuses with TargetCheckedOutDirty before any ref change, naming the path, the change count and the tip the target is still at. Untracked files count, because an untracked file exists nowhere else. The guidance is commit or stash with an explicit "do NOT reset or check it out over"; tests assert no reset or read-tree recipe can appear in that text.
- A holder that is still clean is advanced by git's two-tree `read-tree -m -u <old_tip> <new_tip>`, which refuses when an entry is not up to date, so the decision is git's at the moment it writes rather than ours from an earlier check. Identity is re-verified at write time, so a checkout switched to another branch or detached is left alone with the branch it moved to named.
- Any refusal to refresh reaches the operator: notes are recorded and drained by append_stale_checkout_notes into the same receipt that carries the reconcile line, stating the ref advance, that the refresh declined, git's reason, and that nothing was overwritten — and deliberately not claiming what that checkout now contains, which is unknowable. A poisoned notes mutex recovers its contents instead of dropping safety warnings.
- The merge still succeeds rather than becoming a retryable failure after a committed merge.

GH #73 CANNOT REGRESS, verified through the venue split rather than assumed: a shared checkout on the target takes MergeVenue::SharedCheckout and merges in place, and one on any other branch never holds the target, so the new refusal is unreachable there. merging_still_leaves_the_primary_checkout_untouched_when_no_sibling_holds_the_target asserts unrelated residue still merges, the primary branch does not move, and the merged file is not checked out into it.

task_title: Resolve assembled release retrieval precision regression without weakening oracle
close_reason:
The assembled 3.17.0 candidate meets the committed retrieval baseline again, by an explained correction rather than a lowered bar. The oracle is untouched: baseline.json and REGRESSION_TOLERANCE were never edited and the rebaseline path was never run.

REPRODUCED FIRST, exactly as reported: retrieval_eval_test.rs:1011, ambient_packet live_tiers and all_working, precision@5 0.0714 -> 0.0565, 20.8% relative against a 10% tolerance.

ROOT CAUSE, established with row-level evidence rather than inference. A detached scratch worktree at the pre-change commit 600288d1 ran the identical diagnostic over a byte-identical fixture, so code was the only variable, and it reproduced the committed baseline exactly (P@5 0.071429, 8 hitting cases, mean_returned 1.428571, 24 silent). Against that, the entire -0.8334 precision mass delta was three cases: n01 0.500 -> 0.000, c12 and n02 0.500 -> 0.333. The lost hit was n01, whose task is cas-096e: its packet went from ['2026-08-07-8','2026-08-06-13'] to EMPTY, dropping a memory tagged cas-096e whose body opens "CI wall-clock work on cas-src (cas-096e/GH #142 ...)" — that case's own prior learnings, correctly labelled relevant. So this was a product regression, not a stale oracle. Mechanism: cas-fa938 rightly stopped structural identity terms manufacturing relevance, but `task=` was filtered out of query terms while `binding` only tested query.task_id == row.id, which is true for the task row itself and never for a memory ABOUT that task. Such a row was neither a lexical term nor structurally bound, so it was unreachable. An early expiry hypothesis was disproved and withdrawn: the fixture carries no valid_until and the materialiser never sets one, so the staleness comparison cannot move it, and entries are seeded as created = now - age_days - position, so wall-clock drift shifts all ages together and is not a confound.

CORRECTION, two narrow parts because the first alone measured as inert. names_current_task lets an exact, token-bounded occurrence of the CURRENT task id contribute binding only; and the retriever additionally reads rows naming that id, since binding could not rescue a row the SQL prefilter never fetched. Identity buys retrieval and binding, never a lexical score: scoring terms are unchanged, and staleness, expiry, privacy and eligibility all still apply. Supplemental rows are filtered by the same exact binding rule before the union, so a substring SQL match cannot introduce unbound noise; deduplication is keyed on (surface, id) because ids are unique only within their own table; and the token scan uses match_indices, so a multi-byte task id or body cannot panic on a character boundary.

RESULT, same fixture and diagnostic across all three trees: precision@5 0.071429 baseline -> 0.056548 broken -> 0.090774 fixed, recall@5 0.033801 -> 0.030825 -> 0.050765, cases with a hit 8 -> 7 -> 11, silent 24 -> 20 -> 17. task_title: Skill frontmatter can emit invalid YAML: duplicated escape_yaml leaves backslashes raw in both live writers
close_reason:
Generated frontmatter is now produced by one proven serializer and read back by a parser, so a description like `Use C:\project: inspect` no longer emits YAML that a reader rejects with `found unknown escape character 'p'`.

ROOT CAUSE: three hand-rolled `escape_yaml` copies — cas-cli/src/sync/skills.rs, crates/cas-core/src/sync/skills.rs and crates/cas-core/src/sync/specs.rs — had already drifted, the spec copy escaping backslashes while the skill copies left them raw inside a quoted scalar.

SHARED SEAM: crates/cas-core/src/sync/yaml_scalar.rs exposes cas_core::sync::yaml_scalar and serves all three writers, each keeping its local escape_yaml as a one-line delegate so call sites and harness-specific metadata policy are untouched. Neither SkillSyncer is deleted. serde_yaml 0.9 was added to cas-core; it was already in the tree via cas-cli, so Cargo.lock gains a single edge rather than a package. Every escaping path is a real serializer: serde_yaml emits whenever it can do so on one line, and serde_json — already a cas-core dependency — produces the single-line form otherwise, because a JSON string literal is a valid YAML double-quoted scalar. That claim is proven against a YAML parser over the whole corpus, not asserted. Serializing a &str cannot fail, so the invariant is stated with expect rather than swallowed into an empty scalar that would blank a description.

READER: extract_yaml_value parses the frontmatter and looks the key up exactly, preserving the typed-field behaviour callers depend on — a YAML boolean reads back as "true"/"false" text because user-invocable and disable-model-invocation are compared as those strings, while a sequence, mapping or null reads as absent. Legacy recovery runs only when the parser rejects the document AND matches an unindented line whose key is followed immediately by ':', so an unrelated malformed document cannot answer `description` from `description_extra` and an indented key nested under `hooks:` is not lifted out.

TWO LATENT DEFECTS FIXED BEYOND THE REPORT, both surfaced because a real emitter replaced the hand-rolled one: `argument-hint: [title]` was emitted unquoted, so YAML read it as a one-element sequence rather than the string consumers expect, and quoted values now take whichever quoting the emitter chooses. The three tests that pinned the broken bytes assert the parsed value instead.

task_title: web-fallback endpoint: require proof-of-phone-control (public unauth route grants free audits + enables phone-spoofing)
close_reason:
Free-audit mint budget on per-IP + global daily axes (non-fabricable), charged only on actual mint, all fail-closed; 8 red pre-change tests; jest 802 + bootstrap-smoke green. AC3 met; AC1/AC2 void per ruling; spoofed-phone half → cas-d690.

DETAIL FOR THE RECORD.

The defect: poc.service.ts:315 grants any workspace with owner===null && !hasReceivedFreeAudit one free PAID audit for its lifetime, and sms-responder.service.ts:879 skips the affordability pre-check on the same condition. The public @Public() web-fallback route mints exactly such a workspace for any phone string it has not seen, so the real economic bound was ONE FREE PAID AUDIT PER DISTINCT PHONE STRING — an identity the attacker mints for free by inventing an E.164 string. The pre-existing per-phone limit therefore capped an axis the attacker owns: a speed limit, not a cap. The window counters bounded the rate and never the total.

The fix: a mint budget on per-IP-per-day (WEB_FALLBACK_MINT_IP_DAILY_MAX, default 3) and GLOBAL-per-day (WEB_FALLBACK_MINT_GLOBAL_DAILY_MAX, default 200). Charged ONLY when the submission would actually mint — the phone has neither an existing workspace nor an existing account, mirroring the two skip conditions in ensureWorkspaceForPhoneUnowned. Every other property follows from that exemption: a returning submitter is never charged, so exhausting the global budget pauses NEW mints and cannot lock out anyone already in the funnel; the per-IP cap is checked FIRST and short-circuits WITHOUT touching the global counter, so one capped IP cannot drain the day's budget and take the non-US funnel down with it; a malformed phone is not charged, so garbage is not a cheap way to exhaust the cap. Both counters and the eligibility lookup FAIL CLOSED (503). Enforced in the GUARD, before the handler, so a refused submission leaves no CRM lead, no sms_messages row, no workspace. It runs after the window limits deliberately — it costs up to two indexed DB reads and an unauthenticated caller must not be able to aim those at the database at will. A global-cap bind logs at ERROR; legitimate volume is ~19 new phones/day (562 submissions / 552 distinct phones over 30d), so 200/day is ~10x headroom and a bind means attack or growth.

REUSE, NOT A SECOND MECHANISM (the supervisor's reconciliation instruction): this adds NO new proof-of-identity primitive and does not touch cas-57f1's claim path. cas-57f1's server-issued signed claim token remains the possession proof; cas-0070 adds only the mint-path cost cap, which cas-57f1's own note assigned here ("Minting is separately capped by cas-0070"). No OTP, no country-dependent SMS wall, so Daniel's cas-e8c6 ruling is untouched and no international friction is reintroduced.

Deliberately NOT touched: debitPostAudit's per-workspace lifetime grant also serves the real inbound-SMS funnel; narrowing it there would change behaviour for users this task is not about.

EVIDENCE, no proxy checks. New src/sms/web-fallback-rate-limit.guard.spec.ts (the guard had NO unit spec before). Against the PRE-change guard: 8 failed, 6 passed, 14 total. The 8 red are the evidence — per-IP cap, global-not-charged-after-IP-refusal, global cap, under-both-caps charges both axes, day bucketing, fail-closed on lookup, fail-closed on counter, non-positive-cap config rejection. Stated rather than counted: the 3 exemption/malformed cases passed pre-change VACUOUSLY (no mint keys existed to touch) and the 3 window cases are regression pins. Post-change 14/14. task_title: web-fallback endpoint: require proof-of-phone-control (public unauth route grants free audits + enables phone-spoofing)

DETAIL FOR THE RECORD.

The defect: poc.service.ts:315 grants any workspace with owner===null && !hasReceivedFreeAudit one free PAID audit for its lifetime, and sms-responder.service.ts:879 skips the affordability pre-check on the same condition. The public @Public() web-fallback route mints exactly such a workspace for any phone string it has not seen, so the real economic bound was ONE FREE PAID AUDIT PER DISTINCT PHONE STRING — an identity the attacker mints for free by inventing an E.164 string. The pre-existing per-phone limit therefore capped an axis the attacker owns: a speed limit, not a cap. The window counters bounded the rate and never the total.

The fix: a mint budget on per-IP-per-day (WEB_FALLBACK_MINT_IP_DAILY_MAX, default 3) and GLOBAL-per-day (WEB_FALLBACK_MINT_GLOBAL_DAILY_MAX, default 200). Charged ONLY when the submission would actually mint — the phone has neither an existing workspace nor an existing account, mirroring the two skip conditions in ensureWorkspaceForPhoneUnowned. Every other property follows from that exemption: a returning submitter is never charged, so exhausting the global budget pauses NEW mints and cannot lock out anyone already in the funnel; the per-IP cap is checked FIRST and short-circuits WITHOUT touching the global counter, so one capped IP cannot drain the day's budget and take the non-US funnel down with it; a malformed phone is not charged, so garbage is not a cheap way to exhaust the cap. Both counters and the eligibility lookup FAIL CLOSED (503). Enforced in the GUARD, before the handler, so a refused submission leaves no CRM lead, no sms_messages row, no workspace. It runs after the window limits deliberately — it costs up to two indexed DB reads and an unauthenticated caller must not be able to aim those at the database at will. A global-cap bind logs at ERROR; legitimate volume is ~19 new phones/day (562 submissions / 552 distinct phones over 30d), so 200/day is ~10x headroom and a bind means attack or growth.

REUSE, NOT A SECOND MECHANISM (the supervisor's reconciliation instruction): this adds NO new proof-of-identity primitive and does not touch cas-57f1's claim path. cas-57f1's server-issued signed claim token remains the possession proof; cas-0070 adds only the mint-path cost cap, which cas-57f1's own note assigned here ("Minting is separately capped by cas-0070"). task_title: audit page watcher fires on every store update — add concurrency guard
close_reason:
Coalesce audit-page silent refreshes: primitive postId:status watch key + coalescing runner (queue-one, not drop) + loading-watch drain for the first-load race; 10 same-status emits → 1 fetch, real-store RED/GREEN, 1991 tests green.

Root cause was sharper than the ticket had it: the watcher source was the PostUpdate OBJECT, and applyUpdates overwrites on `updatedAt >=` — note >=, not >. Every poll tick that re-reports the post installs a brand-new object with identical contents, so a reference watch re-fires on each cursor-driven re-emit. Never really about status filtering; object identity churned on every emit.

Did BOTH options the ticket offered, since AC1 and AC2 are separate requirements. Option 2: watch `${postId}:${status}`, a primitive, so Vue dedupes by value; postId in the key so switching between two posts sharing a status is not swallowed. Option 1: every silent refresh routes through createCoalescedRefresh, which serialises passes — relevant because there are TWO independent silent callers, this watcher and a 5s processing poll, so a fetch slower than the interval could be overtaken.

Coalesce, not drop: a request landing mid-flight may reflect a status that did not exist when the in-flight fetch was issued, so discarding it strands the page on a stale status at the final transition. One follow-up pass is sufficient and bounded (burst of N → 1).

Two further holes closed while wiring it: (a) the runner drains its own queue when one of ITS passes settles, but a request deferred by the non-silent initial load has no such pass to wait on — added a watch(loading) drain, else a transition arriving during first load hangs forever on an audit with no processing poll; (b) starting a pass must clear `queued`, else an isBusy-deferred request fires a redundant second pass.

Helpers live in utils/post-refresh.ts so they are testable: the page is ~1300 lines wired to Quasar/Nuxt/PostHog, mounting it to count fetches is mostly stub-wrangling, and source-text assertions pin the code we happened to write rather than the behaviour.

task_title: Re-walk F3: refreshing /create loses a workspace-created draft from view — ?itemId= only resolves items with sourcePostAuditId
close_reason:
Merged into epic/epic-create-conversational-workspace-remediation-b-cas-397c @ bccc3c379 (supervisor merge of factory/brave-salmon-78 @ 2e38580f6). Verified reachable: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2e38580f6 bccc3c379` passes, and the four files land on the epic tip with exactly the diff I authored (composable +51, create.vue +90, en.json +1, es.json +1). cas-68cc, merged in the same window, touched only backend files — `git log 028aa1d6e..bccc3c379 -- useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.ts` lists my commit alone, so there was no interaction on the shared composable. Frontend-only; no backend change was needed.

ROOT CAUSE — two independent halves, both required. The task brief named the first; the second was mine to find, and without it the first is inert.
1. create.vue:200-206 built `auditedSources` from useRecentWork filtered on `entry.sourcePostAuditId`; create.vue:259-267 resolved `route.query.itemId` ONLY against that list and fell through to `?? null` on a miss. `ensureSource` (useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.ts:917) POSTs an item with no audit, so the draft /create makes for itself could never be in the list.
2. Nothing ever wrote `?itemId=` into the URL after ensureSource, so a working resolver would still have had nothing to resolve after a first send.

FIX
- `resolveSourceById(itemId)` on the composable: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/items?itemIds=<id>&limit=1, unwrapped with the existing `unwrapListPayload`; returns {itemId, projectSlug, title} or null when the row has no project slug, so a /p/null/i/<id> route can never be synthesised. Id-only by necessity: [itemId].vue:74 links back with {path:'/create', query:{itemId}} and carries no slug, so anything needing the slug up front could not serve the return path either.
- create.vue resolution: audited list first (no request), otherwise one lookup per id guarded by `attemptedItemIds`; a throw releases the id so a transient failure stays retryable; a stale in-flight answer is dropped when routeItemId no longer matches.
- URL sync via `router.replace` (not push, so Back does not land on an itemId-less /create); preserves the rest of the query; removes itemId when the select is cleared; deliberately silent while nothing has ever been selected, or it would delete the very id being resolved.
- `sourceOptions` offers the resolved draft in the q-select so the control does not read as empty after a reload.
- New locale key `creativeWorkspace.draftSourceTitle` (en + es) names the draft on BOTH the POST and the read-back, replacing the hardcoded English 'Creative workspace draft' literal that was in ensureSource.

NO BACKEND CHANGE — verified, not assumed: workspace-items.controller.ts:187/239 already normalizes `itemIds`; items.service.ts:1325 sets where.id={in:itemIds} while KEEPING where.project.workspaceId from :1319, so the id filter cannot cross workspaces; project.slug is in the include at :1780. The same endpoint is already consumed in production by the recent-work feed.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- URL carries ?itemId=<created id> after a first send — "writes ?itemId= into the URL when the first send creates the item" asserts router.replace with the created id; a companion test asserts the rest of the query survives and itemId is dropped on clear.
- Reload re-hydrates the thread from the server session, tested with a NON-AUDITED item — covered on both layers: the page test asserts resolveSourceById is called and loadSession runs; the composable test drives the real loadSession path and asserts the transcript turn comes back.
- returnTo=creative-workspace lands on the same conversation — a test mounts with id-only query, resolves, clicks Done, and asserts push to /p/acme/i/draft-7?tab=context&returnTo=creative-workspace.
- Suites + typecheck green with real exit codes — below.

RED-FIRST: all 13 tests written and run before implementation. 6 composable tests failed with "resolveSourceById is not a function"; 6 of 7 page tests failed (resolveSourceById never called, replace never called, modelValue null). The 7th — "takes the audited list first and never asks the server for an id it already has" — passed at red on purpose; it is the regression guard on the path that already worked.

1. Vacuous-assertion trap, closed: the locale test would have passed with NO localization at all, because t() over en.json returns the same literal the code could have hardcoded. It now asserts the title is not the dotted key AND that es differs from en, so a missing es entry fails.

close_reason:
F9 fixed in three places, in the order the defect happens. Work commits 14818ef64 (the fix) + cee75782d (supervisor guard tests), branch tip cee75782d, merged into the epic at f144b790f and 560ab7736. AC 1 — "change the framework to listicle" locks framework="Listicle / Steps" as user_provided, receipt updates, copy is correct, deferred script waits for yes.
NEW pure module apps/backend/src/items/idea-chat/creative-workspace-explicit-value.ts: resolveExplicitCreativeFieldLock({message, targets}) matches the message against the framework catalogue (framework-options.ts) and the format catalogue (format-options.ts). Guards, each with its own test: a SET cue must be present ("change … to", "use", "switch to", "make it", "go with", "i want"); option-seeking phrasing ("options", "suggest", "a few", "what are") vetoes the lock; aliases under 5 characters are rejected (PAS/BAB/Q&A collide with ordinary prose — those stay card-only, which is unambiguous by construction); the Unknown and "Hybrid / Multiple" placeholders are never lockable; matching is word-boundary over space-padded normalized forms, longest alias wins. idea-chat.service.ts gains applyExplicitCreativeFieldLock: writes the draft through the existing applySuggestionToDraft (so a format lock still gets its formatOptionId), records the component with provenance user_provided and immediately accepts it via acceptCreativeCandidate — which is what marks the previous version superseded — locks the phase session, and pushes the value to the item column via applyDraftFieldToItem. When the whole running half of the ask was a named value, executeCreativeWorkspaceIntent returns before any audit work and never calls the capability service. When a lock is mixed with real generation, the lock is applied BEFORE the generation loop so the generation is briefed on the framework the creator chose, and its phase is filtered out of `phases`.

AC 2 — candidates generated for a locked field render, and the prior receipt shows superseded.
ROOT CAUSE, file:line: apps/frontend/app/src/utils/project-creative-workspace-thread.ts:317-345 (old) collapsed the LATEST option group for a field into a receipt whenever isCreativeDraftValueSet(field, draftValue). framework was already "Do This, Not That", so the fresh group (Listicle / Steps, Mistakes to Avoid, Unpopular Opinion, Framework Breakdown) was replaced by a receipt of the OLD value — no "Listicle" anywhere in the thread, receipt unchanged, exactly what was measured. The projector now tracks lockIndex per field: the last thing that produced the CURRENT value (the group it was picked from, or a threadReceipt anchor). A group after that index is the live question and renders as cards; the group that owns the value collapses into its receipt and is marked superseded while fresher cards are on screen. Ownership is decided by new exported optionsOwnValue, deliberately forgiving (either normalized string containing the other) so an appended or reformatted applied value still collapses — a "no" is reserved for a group that plainly has nothing to do with the locked value. The ordinary collapse grammar is pinned by an explicit regression test.

AC 3 — the confirmation never claims an update that did not persist, tested on both paths.
CreativeWorkspaceQuestionTemplateKey gains 'multi_intent_selection'. resolveCreativeWorkspaceSequencing takes lockedTargets; the first target having LOCKED is the only thing that authorizes "That's {first} updated". Otherwise the beat is "Here are a few {first} — pick one and I'll redo {rest} to match." New locale keys in en.json AND es.json: creativeWorkspace.thread.confirmation.multiIntentSelection plus a targetsPlural block (the selection beat needs a plural noun; the confirmation beat names one field). The generated result carries lockedFields; the composable appends a threadReceipt anchor per locked field — the same mechanism selectFormat already uses at useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.ts:822 — because a lock has no option group to collapse and would otherwise change the draft with nothing on screen.

DELIBERATE CHANGE TO AN EXISTING TEST. creative-workspace-execution.spec.ts "runs only the first target of a destructive multi-intent request…" used the F9 message verbatim ("Change the framework to listicle and write a new script") and asserted that the framework phase GENERATED and that the beat said multi_intent_confirmation. Its message is now "Change the framework and write a new script" (no named value), so it still covers the D3 sequencing rule on the branch where generation is correct, and it additionally asserts multi_intent_selection and that the copy does not contain "updated". The F9 message is covered by the new test directly below it, which asserts capability.generate was never called, the draft framework is "Listicle / Steps", provenance is user_provided + accepted, framework-original is superseded, workingDraft.componentVersionIds.framework points at the new component, lockedFields is returned, the beat is multi_intent_confirmation, and pendingRequest is {targets:['script'], awaitingConfirmation:true}.

I probed all four target combinations with a throwaway spec and read the actual return values before asserting, rather than writing a test and presenting it as a fix. Verified reachable — `git merge-base --is-ancestor 03030e752 1b57c8c4d` passes, and the file on the epic tip carries the hoisted import at line 153 with `mounted.push(wrapper)` at 157, i.e. the atomic mount/register pair that is the whole fix. Test-only: one file, 26 insertions / 1 deletion.

ROOT CAUSE — and the brief's hypothesis was wrong, which I established before moving on rather than after. The task said to bisect file order for what leaks IN. Nothing leaks in: the file poisons itself, and both reported symptoms are ONE defect.

RULED OUT FIRST: cross-file globalThis clobbering. This file does `Object.assign(globalThis, {onMounted, ...})` at module load, and two other files install a SYNCHRONOUS immediate-invoke onMounted on that same global (create.test.ts:205, workspace-hydration.test.ts:57) — a textbook candidate. Ran all three under `--no-isolate --no-file-parallelism`, one shared context with isolation fully off: 36/36 pass. Vitest never runs two files concurrently in one context, so those beforeEach writes cannot interleave. A file-order bisect would have chased this for nothing.

ACTUAL MECHANISM: `mountCounter` did slow async work BEFORE registering the wrapper for cleanup —
    const CreditBalance = (await import('~/components/CreditBalance.vue')).default;  // slow
    const wrapper = mount(...);
    mounted.push(wrapper);   // registration AFTER the await

Symptom 1 (5000ms timeout): the SFC transform sat inside the first test's budget. Measured — isolation 568ms; full parallel load 848 / 1408 / 1041ms; the other eight tests flat at 3-23ms throughout. Only the first test's duration scales with contention, because only it pays the transform. On a box busier than this idle 32-core one, breaching 5000ms is a matter of degree, not kind.

Symptom 2 ("expected 1 call, got 2") is symptom 1's collateral: a vitest timeout fails the test and runs afterEach but CANNOT cancel the promise. The abandoned continuation still mounts the component and pushes it into `mounted` after cleanup already drained the array. That orphan keeps a live watcher on the shared module-level workspaceRef, so the next test to hydrate a workspace records two loadEntitlementWindow calls.

PROVEN, NOT INFERRED. A purpose-built probe (run, then deleted — not shipped) reproduced the reported signature deterministically:
    PROBE mounted-registry size: 2
    PROBE fetches: [{"force":false,"workspaceId":"ws_1"},{"force":false,"workspaceId":"ws_1"}]
    AssertionError: expected [...] to have a length of 1 but got 2
Verbatim the bug report's second failure.

FIX: hoist the import to module load so `mount` and `mounted.push` occupy the same synchronous tick with no await between them. Kills the trigger (no transform inside a test budget) and the cascade (no suspension point where a timeout can separate a live component from its cleanup). ESM caches the module either way, so it is not a behaviour change — every test still mounts a fresh instance. The in-file comment states the invariant and warns that re-introducing an await in that gap re-introduces the flake.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Root cause identified and documented (which state leaks and from where): above, plus a discovery note on the task. The leaked state is a live Vue watcher held by an orphaned component instance on the file's own module-level refs; the source is the file's own timed-out test, not another file.

- No retry/annotation-based suppression: none. No `retry`, no `.skip`, no timeout bump — the timeout is untouched at its default; the work simply no longer happens inside it.

Merged into epic/epic-create-conversational-workspace-remediation-b-cas-397c @ bccc3c379 (supervisor merge of factory/brave-salmon-78 @ 2e38580f6). Verified reachable: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2e38580f6 bccc3c379` passes, and the four files land on the epic tip with exactly the diff I authored (composable +51, create.vue +90, en.json +1, es.json +1). cas-68cc, merged in the same window, touched only backend files — `git log 028aa1d6e..bccc3c379 -- useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.ts` lists my commit alone, so there was no interaction on the shared composable. Frontend-only; no backend change was needed.

ROOT CAUSE — two independent halves, both required. The task brief named the first; the second was mine to find, and without it the first is inert.
1. create.vue:200-206 built `auditedSources` from useRecentWork filtered on `entry.sourcePostAuditId`; create.vue:259-267 resolved `route.query.itemId` ONLY against that list and fell through to `?? null` on a miss. `ensureSource` (useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.ts:917) POSTs an item with no audit, so the draft /create makes for itself could never be in the list.
2. Nothing ever wrote `?itemId=` into the URL after ensureSource, so a working resolver would still have had nothing to resolve after a first send.

FIX
- `resolveSourceById(itemId)` on the composable: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/items?itemIds=<id>&limit=1, unwrapped with the existing `unwrapListPayload`; returns {itemId, projectSlug, title} or null when the row has no project slug, so a /p/null/i/<id> route can never be synthesised. Id-only by necessity: [itemId].vue:74 links back with {path:'/create', query:{itemId}} and carries no slug, so anything needing the slug up front could not serve the return path either.
- create.vue resolution: audited list first (no request), otherwise one lookup per id guarded by `attemptedItemIds`; a throw releases the id so a transient failure stays retryable; a stale in-flight answer is dropped when routeItemId no longer matches.
- URL sync via `router.replace` (not push, so Back does not land on an itemId-less /create); preserves the rest of the query; removes itemId when the select is cleared; deliberately silent while nothing has ever been selected, or it would delete the very id being resolved.
- `sourceOptions` offers the resolved draft in the q-select so the control does not read as empty after a reload.
- New locale key `creativeWorkspace.draftSourceTitle` (en + es) names the draft on BOTH the POST and the read-back, replacing the hardcoded English 'Creative workspace draft' literal that was in ensureSource.

NO BACKEND CHANGE — verified, not assumed: workspace-items.controller.ts:187/239 already normalizes `itemIds`; items.service.ts:1325 sets where.id={in:itemIds} while KEEPING where.project.workspaceId from :1319, so the id filter cannot cross workspaces; project.slug is in the include at :1780. The same endpoint is already consumed in production by the recent-work feed.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- URL carries ?itemId=<created id> after a first send — "writes ?itemId= into the URL when the first send creates the item" asserts router.replace with the created id; a companion test asserts the rest of the query survives and itemId is dropped on clear.
- Reload re-hydrates the thread from the server session, tested with a NON-AUDITED item — covered on both layers: the page test asserts resolveSourceById is called and loadSession runs; the composable test drives the real loadSession path and asserts the transcript turn comes back.
- returnTo=creative-workspace lands on the same conversation — a test mounts with id-only query, resolves, clicks Done, and asserts push to /p/acme/i/draft-7?tab=context&returnTo=creative-workspace.
- Suites + typecheck green with real exit codes — below.

RED-FIRST: all 13 tests written and run before implementation. 6 composable tests failed with "resolveSourceById is not a function"; 6 of 7 page tests failed (resolveSourceById never called, replace never called, modelValue null). The 7th — "takes the audited list first and never asks the server for an id it already has" — passed at red on purpose; it is the regression guard on the path that already worked.

TWO THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD
1. Vacuous-assertion trap, closed: the locale test would have passed with NO localization at all, because t() over en.json returns the same literal the code could have hardcoded. It now asserts the title is not the dotted key AND that es differs from en, so a missing es entry fails.
2. Dependency-resolution trap, caught late: the worktree had no root/backend node_modules, so my first verification run resolved vite/vitest/nuxt UPWARD into the main checkout's root node_modules, whose lockfile (ca88eec7…) differs from this worktree's (4890c8eb…). Every number I had reported was measured against a tree I had not proven was the right one — the proxy-check shape. I ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (exit 0; its success under --frozen-lockfile is itself proof the worktree lockfile matches its package.json set) and re-ran everything. All results identical, because the lockfile delta is backend-only (body-parser, express-rate-limit, eventsource) and I exercised none of it — luck in part, not design, which is why re-measuring beat reasoning about it.

task_title: Re-walk 2 F11: the pre-flight generation gate runs before the explicit-value lock — "change the framework to listicle and write a new script" with no framework locked returns blocked_script + framework cards instead of locking Listicle / Steps
close_reason:
F11 fixed: the explicit-value lock now resolves and applies BEFORE the pre-flight gate. Commit 6a1e32514, merged into the epic at caad40dd6. Epic tip 560ab7736 was synced first (my merge fast-forwarded to 7091ec724, which is the same tip the supervisor later named — so notification 10711 was already satisfied). 4 files, +383/-61.

Verified on the epic TREE, not just by ancestry: in the merged idea-chat.service.ts, resolveExplicitCreativeFieldLock is at line 1075 and resolveCreativeWorkspaceGenerationGate at 1104 — the order is inverted from the defect. The blocked union member carries lockedFields, and both walk-2 tests are present in the merged spec.

WHAT WAS WRONG. resolveCreativeWorkspaceGenerationGate ran at ~1044 and the lock at ~1107, so for "I actually want to change the framework to be listicle and want a new script" with framework null, the script's framework dependency was judged against a draft that did not yet contain the framework the creator had just named in the same sentence. cas-4a93 only covered the already-locked case, where the gate passed for the wrong reason. Moving the lock above the gate means the gate judges the post-lock draft and can no longer demand a dependency the same message supplies.

THE NON-OBVIOUS HALF, now a code comment so it survives the next edit. Sequencing deliberately stays on the PRE-lock draft. It decides whether a request would destroy work that already existed, and the value being written is not such work. Had I resolved it after applying the lock, targetOverwritesLockedField would see the framework just written, judge the request destructive, and defer the script behind a confirmation — turning one sentence into two turns for a creator who asked for one. Test (a) pins this: capability.generate called ONCE for scriptNotes, question null, pendingRequest null.

BLOCKED TURNS CAN NOW HAVE WRITTEN SOMETHING. "use direct to camera and write a script" locks the format and is then gated on the framework, so the blocked union member gained an optional lockedFields and the service passes it. Without it the format would change with nothing in the thread to show for it — the F9 defect reproduced on the blocked path. No client change was needed: ConversationResult.lockedFields and the appendResultTurns anchor loop built in cas-4a93 are not kind-gated, so they handled a blocked result the moment the backend began sending it.

AC BY AC.
- Lock applied before the pre-flight gate and before pending-request bookkeeping: yes, both walk cases through the real executeCreativeWorkspaceIntent. (a) framework null + the F9 message → framework locked user_provided, lockedFields ['framework'], script generated in the SAME pass, no blocked result. (b) format null + "use direct to camera and write a script" → formatType direct_to_camera + formatOptionId direct_60s written, then kind:'blocked' templateKey blocked_script with missingTargets ['framework'] and a message that does not mention the format, plus lockedFields ['formatType'].
- No stale pendingRequest replaying a dependency prompt after the lock: test (a) asserts pendingRequest is null; the frontend test asserts the resume sends 'Choose a framework' and that 'Choose a format' is never sent — the format is no longer missing, so replaying it would be the stale prompt.
- Existing F9 tests green, unmodified.

RED-FIRST EVIDENCE, stated exactly rather than rounded up.
Backend — both tests were written first and failed against the unmodified service, reproducing the staging symptom. Re-confirmed after the fix by stashing the two source files: "locks a named framework BEFORE the script gate judges the draft (walk 2 F11)" and "locks a named format first, then gates the script on what is STILL missing" both fail, 6 pass. Restored → 8/8.
Frontend — "anchors the locked receipt and resumes on the dependency that is still missing" PASSED AT RED and I am NOT counting it as red. The client already handled lockedFields on any result kind, and the test drives a mocked blocked result, so it proves the contract end-to-end but not new client behaviour. The backend change is what makes it reachable in production.

TWO THINGS THE TESTS TAUGHT ME, recorded rather than papered over.
1. Case (b) needs applyFormatEnabled: true or the format gate is not live at all — and with it true, hydrateDraftFormatFromItem runs for real and calls this.prisma.item.update. I gave the fixture a prisma stub rather than spying hydrateDraftFormatFromItem away, because the spy would have hidden the very path the test exists to exercise.
2. The first version of the frontend test asserted on raw turns and failed with 2 anchors, not 1: the mock returns the same blocked result for the original send and the resume, so the server reports the lock twice. The projector already de-dupes by field (latestReceiptAnchor), so the SCREEN was correct. I moved the assertion to conversation.threadItems — the projected thread — because "only one FORMAT receipt ever reaches the creator" is the real guarantee and a raw-turn count is not.

| check | exit | result |
| backend `npx jest src/items/idea-chat` | 0 | 36 suites / 547 tests (was 543; +4) |
| backend `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` | 0 | 0 errors |
| frontend `npx vitest run` | 0 | 230 files / 2548 tests (was 2547; +1) |
| frontend `npm run typecheck` | 0 | 0 errors |
| eslint, all 4 touched files | 0 | 0 errors (2 pre-existing non-null-assertion warnings from a sibling lane at 1517/1626) |
| prettier --check, all 4 touched files | 0 | clean |

KNOWN BOUNDARY, deliberately not crossed and raised to the supervisor rather than decided unilaterally: a format-ONLY explicit value still shows cards. isFormatOnlyCreativeIntent returns kind:'format' above the lock, so "use direct to camera" on its own renders the picker instead of locking. That is arguably the same F9 principle, but it changes the main "Choose a format" dependency path that cas-e3b4/cas-4277 had just reworked, and neither AC asked for it. task_title: Re-walk F9: "change the framework to listicle" generates framework candidates that never render, leaves "Do This, Not That" locked, yet the confirmation claims "That's the framework updated"
close_reason:
F9 fixed in three places, in the order the defect happens. Work commits 14818ef64 (the fix) + cee75782d (supervisor guard tests), branch tip cee75782d, merged into the epic at f144b790f and 560ab7736. Verified by ancestry AND by content against the epic tree: resolveExplicitCreativeFieldLock, applyExplicitCreativeFieldLock, optionsOwnValue, the es.json multiIntentSelection key and the guard describe are all present in the merged files. 12 files, +1119/-24, plus a 21-line test-only follow-up.

AC 1 — "change the framework to listicle" locks framework="Listicle / Steps" as user_provided, receipt updates, copy is correct, deferred script waits for yes.
NEW pure module apps/backend/src/items/idea-chat/creative-workspace-explicit-value.ts: resolveExplicitCreativeFieldLock({message, targets}) matches the message against the framework catalogue (framework-options.ts) and the format catalogue (format-options.ts). Guards, each with its own test: a SET cue must be present ("change … to", "use", "switch to", "make it", "go with", "i want"); option-seeking phrasing ("options", "suggest", "a few", "what are") vetoes the lock; aliases under 5 characters are rejected (PAS/BAB/Q&A collide with ordinary prose — those stay card-only, which is unambiguous by construction); the Unknown and "Hybrid / Multiple" placeholders are never lockable; matching is word-boundary over space-padded normalized forms, longest alias wins. idea-chat.service.ts gains applyExplicitCreativeFieldLock: writes the draft through the existing applySuggestionToDraft (so a format lock still gets its formatOptionId), records the component with provenance user_provided and immediately accepts it via acceptCreativeCandidate — which is what marks the previous version superseded — locks the phase session, and pushes the value to the item column via applyDraftFieldToItem. When the whole running half of the ask was a named value, executeCreativeWorkspaceIntent returns before any audit work and never calls the capability service. When a lock is mixed with real generation, the lock is applied BEFORE the generation loop so the generation is briefed on the framework the creator chose, and its phase is filtered out of `phases`.

AC 2 — candidates generated for a locked field render, and the prior receipt shows superseded.
ROOT CAUSE, file:line: apps/frontend/app/src/utils/project-creative-workspace-thread.ts:317-345 (old) collapsed the LATEST option group for a field into a receipt whenever isCreativeDraftValueSet(field, draftValue). framework was already "Do This, Not That", so the fresh group (Listicle / Steps, Mistakes to Avoid, Unpopular Opinion, Framework Breakdown) was replaced by a receipt of the OLD value — no "Listicle" anywhere in the thread, receipt unchanged, exactly what was measured. The projector now tracks lockIndex per field: the last thing that produced the CURRENT value (the group it was picked from, or a threadReceipt anchor). A group after that index is the live question and renders as cards; the group that owns the value collapses into its receipt and is marked superseded while fresher cards are on screen. Ownership is decided by new exported optionsOwnValue, deliberately forgiving (either normalized string containing the other) so an appended or reformatted applied value still collapses — a "no" is reserved for a group that plainly has nothing to do with the locked value. The ordinary collapse grammar is pinned by an explicit regression test.

AC 3 — the confirmation never claims an update that did not persist, tested on both paths.
CreativeWorkspaceQuestionTemplateKey gains 'multi_intent_selection'. resolveCreativeWorkspaceSequencing takes lockedTargets; the first target having LOCKED is the only thing that authorizes "That's {first} updated". Otherwise the beat is "Here are a few {first} — pick one and I'll redo {rest} to match." New locale keys in en.json AND es.json: creativeWorkspace.thread.confirmation.multiIntentSelection plus a targetsPlural block (the selection beat needs a plural noun; the confirmation beat names one field). The generated result carries lockedFields; the composable appends a threadReceipt anchor per locked field — the same mechanism selectFormat already uses at useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.ts:822 — because a lock has no option group to collapse and would otherwise change the draft with nothing on screen.

DELIBERATE CHANGE TO AN EXISTING TEST. creative-workspace-execution.spec.ts "runs only the first target of a destructive multi-intent request…" used the F9 message verbatim ("Change the framework to listicle and write a new script") and asserted that the framework phase GENERATED and that the beat said multi_intent_confirmation. That test encoded the defect. Its message is now "Change the framework and write a new script" (no named value), so it still covers the D3 sequencing rule on the branch where generation is correct, and it additionally asserts multi_intent_selection and that the copy does not contain "updated". The F9 message is covered by the new test directly below it, which asserts capability.generate was never called, the draft framework is "Listicle / Steps", provenance is user_provided + accepted, framework-original is superseded, workingDraft.componentVersionIds.framework points at the new component, lockedFields is returned, the beat is multi_intent_confirmation, and pendingRequest is {targets:['script'], awaitingConfirmation:true}.

SUPERVISOR GUARD (notification 10611), delivered in cee75782d and stated honestly: both messages named — "I want to start based on a text hook" and "now work on a text hook" — ALREADY returned null before the tests were written. I probed all four target combinations with a throwaway spec and read the actual return values before asserting, rather than writing a test and presenting it as a fix. "work on" is not in SET_CUES and neither message contains a catalogue alias. The tests are forward-looking: a future widening of SET_CUES cannot turn an ordinary opening into a silent field write. Each case is asserted three ways — targets ['text_hook'], ['framework','text_hook'], ['format','text_hook'] — so the ALIAS matcher is what rejects them, not the target filter, which is the weaker guarantee a targets-only assertion would have proved.

RED-FIRST EVIDENCE (measured by reverting, not asserted).
Backend — stashed idea-chat.service.ts + creative-workspace-orchestration.ts and moved the new module aside: 3 named tests failed ("only claims an update when the first target actually locked a value", "runs only the first target of a destructive multi-intent request…", "locks the framework the creator named instead of generating candidates for it") and the explicit-value suite failed to resolve at all ("Cannot find module './creative-workspace-explicit-value'"). Restored → green.
Frontend — stashed the projector, the composable and both locale files: 4 of the 6 new tests failed ("renders the new cards and supersedes the receipt of the value they replace", "shows the locked value at its anchor and supersedes the cards it overrode", "renders the selection beat in Spanish too", "anchors a receipt for a field the creator named"). The 2 that stayed green, stated plainly rather than counted as red: "asks for a pick, and never claims an update" passes vacuously at red in English because the old code falls through to the SERVED sentence, which is the same string — the SPANISH test is the real proof for that beat; "still collapses the group the current value was picked from" is a regression guard that must pass both ways by design.

CONFLICT RESOLUTION worth recording. The epic (F3, factory/wild-panther-25) and my branch both appended a describe block to the tail of useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.test.ts and git interleaved them. I inspected all three merge stages before resolving: `git show :1/:2/:3` proved MY side is a pure append to base (1378 → 1482 lines) but THEIRS is not — it also edits mid-file (F6's "names only the dependency that is actually missing in the script gate", base lines 700-746). A naive keep-both-hunks resolution would have silently deleted that test. Resolved as theirs-in-full + my 104-line appendix, verified by 0 conflict markers and by all three describe blocks being present.

VERIFICATION on the merged state — exit codes captured from each command directly, not from a pipe tail.
| check | exit | result |
| backend `npx jest src/items/idea-chat` | 0 | 36 suites / 543 tests |
| backend `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` | 0 | 0 errors |
| frontend `npx vitest run` | 0 | 230 files / 2547 tests |
| frontend `npm run typecheck` (nuxt typecheck) | 0 | 0 errors |
| eslint, every touched file in both apps | 0 | 0 errors (2 pre-existing non-null-assertion warnings from a sibling lane) |
| prettier --check (incl. both locale files) | 0 | clean |
| `npx jest …creative-workspace-explicit-value.spec.ts` after the guard commit | 0 | 14 tests |

The first nuxt typecheck run caught a real defect and is recorded rather than hidden: ThreadReceiptRenderItem.field is the wider Thread union including 'mode', which has no draft column, so lockIndex could not be keyed off a projected receipt. Fixed by recording the anchor's lock index in the main turn loop where the type is exactly IdeaChatField.

WORTH A REVIEWER'S EYE: the lock deliberately errs conservative. A message that names a catalogue value with no set cue, or that also asks for options, still generates cards — a false lock silently overwrites the creator's field, which is a worse failure than one extra question. Format locking is wired through the same generic path as framework but is AC-tested for framework plus three format cases; the format gate, formatOptionId and the select-format endpoint are untouched.

task_title: Re-walk F6: D2 replay fires before the format gate is satisfied, then never again — "start with a text hook" → concept lock → format lock ends with no text hooks (Ben 9:39 still broken)
close_reason:
Frontend-only fix, merged into the epic (fix commit fe4865552, branch tip 827ae7863).

WHAT WAS WRONG (file:line)
1. utils/creative-workspace-gates.ts (old) — the client's missing-dependency rule knew only "script → format+framework" and "hook → concept". It had no twin of the server's creativeRequestNeedsFormat (backend creative-workspace-orchestration.ts:279-289 + FORMAT_EXEMPT_PHASES:266). With pending targets ['text_hook'] and no format, locking the concept made missing=[] → the composable replayed the ask immediately (the single POST /conversation observed at 17:26:37).
2. useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.ts maybeResumePending — the server gated that replay again (blocked_format, the copy printed a second time), but the `replayedMessage === pending.message` guard counted the gated attempt as the one allowed replay, so the format lock produced NO replay. Thread ended on a bold question with zero hooks.

WHAT CHANGED
- creative-workspace-gates.ts: client twin of TARGET_PHASES + FORMAT_EXEMPT_PHASES as creativeTargetsNeedFormat(); missingTargetsForCreativeDraft takes options.formatGateActive and adds format for every non-exempt target (text_hook, caption, edit_suggestions, script, payoff, gabbers_choice — never concept/format/framework). Added nextActionsWithoutLockedDependencies() and creativeDraftHasConcept().
- useCreativeWorkspaceConversation.ts: `formatGateActive` computed reads session.seed.applyFormatEnabled + improvementScope !== 'no_refilm' (GET /session returns the whole session — idea-chat.controller.ts:414); with no seed in the payload it falls back to `formatGateSeen`, set the first time the server itself gated on format. Both signals are needed: seed alone leaves a seedless payload broken; the fallback alone would stall a replay forever in an apply-format-disabled workspace.
- poll(): a `kind:'blocked'` result clears `replayedMessage` — the server said the ask is still pending. resumeBudget is NOT refunded, so the chain still terminates at distinct-targets + 3.
- suggestedReplies: locked dependencies filtered out of the next-action row, applied AFTER the D3 confirmation early-return (those chips exist to redo locked fields).
- Discovery-note copy nit: the script gate uses new blocked.scriptFormat / blocked.scriptFramework keys (en + es) when exactly one dependency is missing, instead of always claiming "I need a format and a framework first".

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- exactly one replay AFTER the format lock, none before → "does not replay the ask while the format is still missing, and replays once after the lock" (send → blocked_format → concept lock: no send → format lock: one replay, generated hooks → later lock: no third send).
- blocked replay resets the guard; budget terminates → "reopens the replay guard when the replay itself comes back blocked" + "gives up after the resume budget when client and server disagree forever" (8 locks, sends capped at 5).
- client rule matches the server → utils/__tests__/creative-workspace-gates.test.ts pins the target→needs-format table target by target, plus gate-inactive, not_set format, script-in-place-of-concept.
- chips never offer a locked dependency → "stops offering 'Choose a format' once the format is locked" plus the util's three chip cases; the sibling's F5 chip tests still pass against the single shared implementation.

The budget test passed at red on purpose: it guards termination the fix must not break.

task_title: Re-walk F1: first send on a fresh /create shows nothing for ~9.5s — ack/session requests wait behind the 7s post-updates long-poll in the frontend request queue
close_reason:
Delivered on factory/agile-cheetah-71 @ 3f4a1729b (branched from epic tip bccc3c379, pushed, merged into the epic at e0633894).

AC 1 — reproduction harness + trace: tests/create-first-send-timing.spec.ts. `nuxt dev` + Playwright with Firebase's password exchange, the token refresh and every /api/v1 call mocked (no credentials, no DB). post-updates held open 7000ms, everything else 120ms; the send fires only after a post-updates request is demonstrably in flight; long tasks captured via a PerformanceObserver armed in addInitScript. The full per-request trace prints on every run. Measured: post-updates in flight from t=-0.00s; ensureSource POST t=+0.09s (0.13s); acknowledge, conversation and session all start at t=+0.25s within 10ms of each other; long tasks >50ms after Enter: NONE; first Gabber text 288-396ms across runs. Conclusion recorded honestly: NO client-side await couples first paint to the poll, the stall did not reproduce, and the mechanism stays UNCONFIRMED (correlated once, n=1). I am not asserting the 9.5s staging sample was caused by the long-poll.

AC 2 — guarantee + serialization removed: the harness asserts first Gabber text < 1500ms with the 7s poll open (382ms on the final run) and stays in the repo. The trace also exposed a real defect the ticket did not know about: one send fired EIGHT recent-work requests inside the ~400ms window the send needs the backend. Root cause composables/useRecentSidebarRefresh.ts:25-51 — any mutating request whose path contains "/items" counts as an item mutation, and every creative-workspace endpoint sits at .../items/:id/idea-chat/..., so /conversation AND /conversation/acknowledge each bumped the refresh token (auth-api.ts:529,599-601) and each of the two mounted recent-work surfaces refetched posts/dashboard + workspace items. Four wasted backend requests per chat turn, forever. Fixed by adding /idea-chat/conversation, /idea-chat/select-format and /idea-chat/edit-applied-field to ITEM_MUTATION_EXCLUSIONS, alongside the legacy generate/refine/select-option entries already there. `POST .../projects/:slug/items` still refreshes — that is what puts a new draft in the recent list. Trade-off (those turns bump updatedAt and the lists sort by it, so the active draft may not re-sort until the next refresh) is documented in the source and matches the call already made for the legacy endpoints.

AC 3 — concurrency budget on inference: untouched. No change to getMaxConcurrentRequests, the auth-api gate, or any flag.

AC 4 — no regression, real exit codes: `npx vitest run app/src/{pages,composables,utils,components}` exit 0, 208 files / 2323 tests pass (includes usePostUpdatesPolling.test.ts and post-updates.test.ts — polling and the notification bell untouched). `npx nuxt typecheck` exit 0, zero TS errors. eslint clean on both changed frontend files.

TEST-FIRST, shown failing in both directions:
- app/src/composables/__tests__/useRecentSidebarRefresh.test.ts (new, 7 cases): 4 FAILED before the fix ("expected true to be false"); the 3 that must keep working (item create, rename, GET) passed both ways. 7/7 after.
- The Playwright collateral assertion was proven to have teeth by reverting the exclusion: 8 requests → FAIL, restored → 4 → PASS.

task_title: SPIKE: why the super-admin Posts page (/dashboard) is slow to load and sometimes freezes (Ben, 2026-09-01)
close_reason:
SPIKE complete. All 5 questions answered with measurements against deployed staging + the Neon staging branch; no product code changed (working tree clean, throwaway specs live only in the artifacts dir).

DOMINANT CAUSE, named with numbers: GET /api/v1/workspaces/all returns 33,081 rows x 36 fields = 29,598,889 bytes (1,336,389 gzipped), unpaginated and uncached (workspace.service.ts:518 — findMany with `include:` and no select/take/where deletedAt). pages/dashboard/index.vue:2115 fires it unconditionally on mount as the FIRST of five serial awaits, solely to populate one dropdown. Feeding that array into a `persist: true` Pinia store (stores/workspace.ts:1230, no pick/omit) blocks the main thread for 4,146-4,728 ms in a SINGLE long task.

Q1 waterfall: /workspaces/all = 1,749 ms wall / 1,328 ms TTFB — 4x the next-slowest request and the only one over a second. Full 16-row table in findings.md.
Q2 server vs client: NEITHER is the DB — EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the equivalent SQL is 45.132 ms, all shared-buffer hits, no missing index. ~1.7 s TTFB is Prisma hydration + JSON.stringify in Node. The client is worse: 4.5 s. CPU-profile ancestry attributes it to (a) 688 ms `serialize` <- `cg` <- `$subscribe.detached` = pinia-plugin-persistedstate, and (b) 661+105 ms Vue deep-watch traverse()/ownKeys Proxy traps. JSON.parse of the 29.6 MB body is only 50 ms, so parsing is NOT the cost.
Q3 "freezes" = one unbroken 4.1-4.7 s main-thread task, measured 4 times. Not a stuck request (all 200) and not table rendering — QSelect virtual-scrolls (30 DOM nodes for 33,081 options; 131 ms to open). Row counts: workspaces 33,081 / projects 33,076 / items 402 / accounts 86.
Q4 yes — it fetches metadata for EVERY workspace before any is selected, but only to fill the chooser; items stay scoped to one workspace. Not necessary: 3 of 36 fields are used, and a 3-field payload is 2,715,022 B (-90.8%).
Q5 SSR adds ZERO — nuxt.config.ts:443 sets '/dashboard/**': { ssr: false }; /dashboard returns an identical 10,688-byte empty shell with AND without a session cookie (TTFB 0.09-0.17 s). useServerSessionVerify in middleware/dashboard.ts is dead code on this route.

CAUSAL PROOF (not inference): trimming only the /workspaces/all response to 50 rows via route interception, interleaved x2 against uncapped controls, drops the longest main-thread block from 4,146/4,728 ms to 132/166 ms (-96.5%) and total blocking from 6,679/5,117 ms to 336/290 ms (-94.6%).

BONUS CORRECTNESS BUG found while measuring: the 29.6 MB store write hits Chrome's ~5 MB localStorage quota, throws QuotaExceededError, and pinia-plugin-persistedstate swallows it silently (debug unset; page console logged zero errors). Consequently all 22 persisted fields of the workspace store — currentWorkspace, workspaceUser, entitlement* — stop being persisted for super admins from the moment /dashboard is opened. Capping the payload makes the write succeed.

ALSO: the task brief's endpoint assumption was wrong — /dashboard never calls /api/v1/posts/dashboard or /posts/dashboard/workspaces. Corrected in the write-up.

RANKED FIX PLAN with cost/benefit/risk, splittable into implementation tasks without further investigation: (0) size prod impact via `SELECT count(*) FROM workspaces` on br-still-credit-adnd0m7z — staging's 33,081 is inflated by a 32,987-row April 2026 seed and prod was excluded by the task's own read-only-staging constraint; (1) explicit 3-field `select:` + `where deletedAt: null` on getAllWorkspaces, -90.8% payload, low risk; (2) `persist: { omit: ['allWorkspaces'] }` — one line, this is the freeze fix and it repairs the silent quota failure; (3) server-side typeahead /workspaces/search replacing the 33k dropdown, medium risk, removes the scaling entirely; (4) parallelize the serial onMounted chain; (5) explicit `select:` on /items (currently ~50-83 KB PER ROW, all 14 JSON blob columns + unbounded comments/attachments); (6) the six unpaged workspace-wide scans in items.service.ts:1864,1905-1970 (payload and bvf_analysis each fetched twice, awaited serially); (7) hygiene incl. the /users 1+2N, the dead WorkspaceContextMiddleware route pattern, and up-to-20 writes inside a GET.

Measurement gaps, recorded as the acceptance criteria permit ("could not measure because X"): prod counts/timings not measured because the task constrained this spike to staging and forbade prod queries; real-hardware wall-clock not measured because all runs were headless Chrome on a dev machine (a mid-range laptop will be worse than the 1x figures); PostHog recorder time is attributed as a consequence rather than an independent cause because it collapsed along with everything else in the A/B. task_title: Make It Mine draft: "View Original Details" link in the post header does nothing
close_reason:
Fixed and verified on DEPLOYED staging: tapping "View Original Details" on a Make It Mine draft opens the original post details at phone width.

Root cause (measured in a real browser, not inferred): below 1024px the item page's own header is display:none and the visible one is layouts/default.vue -> MobileInspectorHeaderBar, whose tap handler is shared Nuxt state written by useRegisterMobileInspectorHeader, not a prop. Vue Router runs the INCOMING page's setup before the outgoing page unmounts, so leaving /audit/<id> for the fresh draft wiped the registration the draft had just installed. Bindings recovered on their own (the item arrives async and re-fires the deep watcher) so the green link still rendered; the handler, watched on a value that never changes, stayed null forever. Arrival-path-specific, not device-specific — and every real Make It Mine run arrives that way. Desktop was unaffected because its header binds @info-click on the page.

Fix: registrations carry an owner (the page's Vue instance uid) and teardown goes through release(owner), a no-op once a later page owns the header. Second half of the AC: itemShowsOriginalPostDetails() (utils/idea-chat-entry.ts) also requires the source audit's CONTENT, not just its id, so a draft whose source post was deleted hides the link instead of opening a drawer of placeholders.

task_title: Backend jest failure on main after the Add Workspace gate: workspace.service.create-integration.spec.ts "creates a distinct explicitly-requested workspace for a phone-backed account"
close_reason:
