Exact scenario: "creates a distinct explicitly-requested workspace for a phone-backed account" seeds a phone-backed owner with _count.ownedWorkspaces=1 and calls createWorkspace({name:'Second Brand', allowAdditionalWorkspace:true}). Under cas-e507 that request is exactly what the plan gate must refuse for an unsubscribed account (403 WORKSPACE_PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED), so the old assertion (a second workspace is minted) no longer states the intended rule.

The proximate failure was narrower than "stale": the spec's in-memory Prisma double has no `workspace.findMany`, which the guard reads (workspace.service.ts:127 evaluateWorkspaceCreationEligibility <- :206 assertCanCreateAdditionalWorkspace <- :358 createWorkspace). The call threw `TypeError: this.prisma.workspace.findMany is not a function`, which createWorkspace's catch wrapped as `BadRequestException: Failed to create workspace: ...` (:645). The double was also self-contradictory — accounts `_count` claimed one owned workspace while `store.workspace` was empty — so a naive findMany would have reported 0 owned and let the gate pass for the wrong reason.

Regression ruled out by reading the gate's precondition `hasExistingWorkspaceAccess && !shouldEnsurePhoneWorkspace` (workspace.service.ts:348-360): phone-first signup with no workspace is not gated (hasExistingWorkspaceAccess=false); the idempotent setup/recovery retry is not gated (shouldEnsurePhoneWorkspace=true); a member of someone else's brand creating their first OWNED workspace passes because eligibility counts only rows with owner=uid, deletedAt=null (0 < limit 1). No legitimate path is newly blocked.

1. getWorkspaceInvoices: `amount` is now `inv.status === 'paid' ? inv.amount_paid : inv.amount_due`. amount_paid is 0 by definition on an unpaid invoice, so a real $7.00 charge rendered "$0.00" — that is why Ben's screenshot read "$0.00 Void" for rows that were $7.00 due (OOHPXFFA-0001/-0002: total 700, amount_due 700, amount_paid 0). FIELD CHOICE, per status and deliberate: paid -> amount_paid (what was handed over); every other visible row -> amount_due rather than total, because amount_due is net of any Stripe customer-balance credit already applied and is therefore the figure the customer is actually asked for. The genuine $0.00 free-month receipt stays $0.00 (cas-272a decided that row stays visible). The same resolved figure now feeds the regional display mapping, which compared amount_paid against the settlement amounts — an unpaid international invoice compared 0, matched neither intro nor recurring, and silently fell back to the bare USD row. That second defect was unreported and is fixed by the same change.
2. createSubscription: an IDENTICAL restart is handed the attempt already in flight — same subscription, same client secret, no cancel, no create, no void. The bar is same price, same buyer, same workspace, same promo context, same market, invoice still `open`, and a matching first-cycle discount. Anything else falls through to the untouched cancel + create. Emits billing.checkoutRestartReused so the rate is visible in prod rather than inferred.

task_title: SPIKE: why the super-admin Posts page (/dashboard) is slow to load and sometimes freezes (Ben, 2026-09-01)
close_reason:
SPIKE complete. All 5 questions answered with measurements against deployed staging + the Neon staging branch; no product code changed (working tree clean, throwaway specs live only in the artifacts dir).

DOMINANT CAUSE, named with numbers: GET /api/v1/workspaces/all returns 33,081 rows x 36 fields = 29,598,889 bytes (1,336,389 gzipped), unpaginated and uncached (workspace.service.ts:518 — findMany with `include:` and no select/take/where deletedAt). pages/dashboard/index.vue:2115 fires it unconditionally on mount as the FIRST of five serial awaits, solely to populate one dropdown. Feeding that array into a `persist: true` Pinia store (stores/workspace.ts:1230, no pick/omit) blocks the main thread for 4,146-4,728 ms in a SINGLE long task.

Q1 waterfall: /workspaces/all = 1,749 ms wall / 1,328 ms TTFB — 4x the next-slowest request and the only one over a second. Full 16-row table in findings.md.
Q2 server vs client: NEITHER is the DB — EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the equivalent SQL is 45.132 ms, all shared-buffer hits, no missing index. ~1.7 s TTFB is Prisma hydration + JSON.stringify in Node. The client is worse: 4.5 s. CPU-profile ancestry attributes it to (a) 688 ms `serialize` <- `cg` <- `$subscribe.detached` = pinia-plugin-persistedstate, and (b) 661+105 ms Vue deep-watch traverse()/ownKeys Proxy traps. JSON.parse of the 29.6 MB body is only 50 ms, so parsing is NOT the cost.
Q3 "freezes" = one unbroken 4.1-4.7 s main-thread task, measured 4 times. Not a stuck request (all 200) and not table rendering — QSelect virtual-scrolls (30 DOM nodes for 33,081 options; 131 ms to open). Row counts: workspaces 33,081 / projects 33,076 / items 402 / accounts 86.
Q4 yes — it fetches metadata for EVERY workspace before any is selected, but only to fill the chooser; items stay scoped to one workspace. Not necessary: 3 of 36 fields are used, and a 3-field payload is 2,715,022 B (-90.8%).
Q5 SSR adds ZERO — nuxt.config.ts:443 sets '/dashboard/**': { ssr: false }; /dashboard returns an identical 10,688-byte empty shell with AND without a session cookie (TTFB 0.09-0.17 s). useServerSessionVerify in middleware/dashboard.ts is dead code on this route.

CAUSAL PROOF (not inference): trimming only the /workspaces/all response to 50 rows via route interception, interleaved x2 against uncapped controls, drops the longest main-thread block from 4,146/4,728 ms to 132/166 ms (-96.5%) and total blocking from 6,679/5,117 ms to 336/290 ms (-94.6%).

BONUS CORRECTNESS BUG found while measuring: the 29.6 MB store write hits Chrome's ~5 MB localStorage quota, throws QuotaExceededError, and pinia-plugin-persistedstate swallows it silently (debug unset; page console logged zero errors). Consequently all 22 persisted fields of the workspace store — currentWorkspace, workspaceUser, entitlement* — stop being persisted for super admins from the moment /dashboard is opened. Capping the payload makes the write succeed.

ALSO: the task brief's endpoint assumption was wrong — /dashboard never calls /api/v1/posts/dashboard or /posts/dashboard/workspaces. Corrected in the write-up.

Root cause (BeginConversation.vue): Cut 1's `tail` renders as one block at the END of the template, after every step section, while Cut 3 renders `acks.*` inside the section for the state and `bridges.*` inside the section they name. Every send's answer therefore rendered above its own receipt, and once the machine advanced the receipt fell below the next step's card.

The fix is the placement model the task specified and nothing else — no new store, no copy, chip, locale or endpoint change: tail entries carry `fromState` (set in `pushTail` from the current view state), each step section renders `entriesFrom(<its state>)` immediately above its own ack, and the end-of-thread block renders `orphanTail` — only turns whose owning section is off screen, so nothing is ever dropped. `sectionOwns()` is the single ownership decision: the five step sections when `hasReached`, `auth_required` always, `auditing` while the reveal block has a phase, everything else falls through to the tail. Two placements needed a judgement call and are commented in the file: the reveal beat's `revealLine` is ONE element that is the question until answered and the ack afterwards, so its receipt renders above it; and `acks.identity` renders outside the auth_required section (it also covers checkout_required), so that receipt slot sits between them.

Root-caused and fixed at source in apps/dm; proven test-first. Merged to the epic as 823aa1fade37.

Root cause: posthtml-expressions escapes `{{ }}` output, and copy written once as `{{ page.t('key') }}` in a component attribute or in front matter is evaluated twice — escaped when the value is computed, then escaped again by the site that prints it. `label="{{ page.t('completion_cta') }}"` became `Set password & view audit` in the attribute, then button.html's `{{ label }}` made it `&amp;`. This is the convention the layout already used for page.title/page.preheader. All 33 such call sites were verified by grep to carry build-time i18n copy only; no raw output was introduced for any runtime variable — names, workspace names and links are written @{{var}} and remain the backend renderer's job. Supervisor review independently confirmed the only non-page.t() value reaching a raw site is error-alert's preheader @{{context}}, which page.preheader already raw-printed before this change. Rewriting the 137 producer-side call sites instead was rejected because it breaks the ~104 single-pass body sites.

task_title: Cut 3b: thread ordering — the user's receipt must render before Gabber's ack and bridge (today "Got it — that's you." appears above "That's me")
close_reason:

Root cause (BeginConversation.vue): Cut 1's `tail` renders as one block at the END of the template, after every step section, while Cut 3 renders `acks.*` inside the section for the state and `bridges.*` inside the section they name. Every send's answer therefore rendered above its own receipt, and once the machine advanced the receipt fell below the next step's card.

The fix is the placement model the task specified and nothing else — no new store, no copy, chip, locale or endpoint change: tail entries carry `fromState` (set in `pushTail` from the current view state), each step section renders `entriesFrom(<its state>)` immediately above its own ack, and the end-of-thread block renders `orphanTail` — only turns whose owning section is off screen, so nothing is ever dropped. `sectionOwns()` is the single ownership decision: the five step sections when `hasReached`, `auth_required` always, `auditing` while the reveal block has a phase, everything else falls through to the tail. Two placements needed a judgement call and are commented in the file: the reveal beat's `revealLine` is ONE element that is the question until answered and the ack afterwards, so its receipt renders above it; and `acks.identity` renders outside the auth_required section (it also covers checkout_required), so that receipt slot sits between them.

task_title: Explore-by-epic, round 2: three genuinely fresh interactive concepts on real data (anti-generic brief; operator rejected the card/tab dashboard)
close_reason:
Three fresh interactive concepts delivered on real data. Merged into the epic branch as df430d4 (worker commit 0eb8cf8), all under docs/design/epic-explorer-round2-2026-08/ with the repo diff confined to that directory, and mirrored to /home/pippenz/.cas/artifacts/cas-b93e/.

THE THREE, one sentence each:
1. THE CASSY RECORD (light-surfaced) — every week of the year is a newspaper front page, and the type size of every headline is the number of child tasks that epic actually shipped; verb: flip.
2. THE CORE SAMPLE (time-driven) — six months of work drilled as a sediment core where depth is time, the thickness of every layer is how many epics were filed that week, and the grains inside it are the epics; verb: drill, with continuous zoom and a hand lens.
3. THE UNSPOOLING (epic→child structure, directly) — every epic hangs as a cord whose length is its real child-task count, and pulling one untwists it into those children as labelled fibres; verb: pull.

RECOMMENDATION: ship THE CORE SAMPLE first — it changes what you know (it makes the shape of the half-year legible in one image: a 41-epic flood bed in late July, a 2-epic hairline in mid-August, a 50%-one-theme week in July, all computed rather than asserted) and it needs nothing the digest pipeline is not already producing (effort M, no dependency on the edge backfill). THE CASSY RECORD second — it is the artefact that gets sent, and the only one of the three that is better on a phone than a list; same effort M. THE UNSPOOLING third and as the epic DETAIL view rather than the index: it is the most beautiful and the only one that answers "what is actually inside this epic", but it is L, it hard-depends on cas-6cad/cas-91b0 landing the edges in the cloud, and a 55-fibre fan wants width so the phone story is a real degradation.

REAL DATA INCLUDING THE EDGES ROUND 1 LACKED: 438 distinct epics (the digest's 446 records contain 8 duplicate ids), 11 projects, 24 weeks 2026-03-16→2026-08-24, and 2,928 real parent→child edges across 368 of the 438 epics — harvested strictly read-only per the supervisor guardrail (each DB copied to a temp file and opened `file:...?mode=ro`), dependencies.dep_type='parent-child' joined to tasks for status/type/dates. Child count min 1 / median 6 / max 55. Note for whoever picks this up: cas-src, ozer and gabber-studio live under /home/pippenz/Petrastella/, not petra_stella_tools/ as the brief assumed — scanning all 36 local DBs is what found them.

FINDINGS THE PROTOTYPES SURFACED (none of which the plain list can show):
- The half-year is wildly uneven: 41 epics filed in the week of 6 Jul and again 27 Jul, versus 2 in the week of 10 Aug.
- Almost nothing takes more than a day: 259 of 371 closed epics have a 0-day span, and 2,170 of 2,602 closed children likewise. That measurement killed "duration as length" as an encoding and is why cord length encodes count.
- 70 of 438 epics have no child tasks at all, and they are NOT an early-history artifact — they are spread evenly across all six months and concentrated by project (34 of them in ozer, i.e. a quarter of ozer's epics run flat).
- The embedding geometry disagrees with the model's own theme labels (cluster 6: 140 points, 60 explorer-UX + 25 onboarding + 20 security, purity 0.43), which is why round 1's decision to facet the scatter by theme destroyed its own most interesting finding.

ANTI-GENERIC COMPLIANCE: no tab bar, no card grid, no sidebar-plus-list, no hero stats row, and no filter control of any kind in any of the three. One metaphor and one gesture each. One light-surfaced (broadsheet: cream paper, IBM Plex Serif, brand palette inverted), one time-driven (core), one showing epic→child directly (unspool). None of round 1's metaphors reused: the embedding layout ships in the bundle but no concept plots it, because re-plotting the rejected scatter would have been the generic move.

New apps/backend/src/posts/instagram-post-date.util.ts: resolveInstagramPostDate() returns {seconds, field}; rawInstagramTakenAt() returns the provider's untouched taken_at. posts.service.ts delegates instagramItemTimestamp to it, mapInstagramPostToItem records the winning field in a new postedAtField, and a log line fires only when a correction moves a date by more than an hour. ALGORITHM, AND WHY IT IS NOT A LITERAL min() OF THE THREE FIELDS
Post date = EARLIEST of the publish-time candidates {caption.created_at (or created_at_utc), taken_at + legacy aliases}. device_timestamp is a last-resort fallback only, never a min() participant. Two measurements from the cas-4567 captures forced this:
1. device_timestamp is a capture time, not a publish time, and its UNITS VARY - microseconds on reels (1784167500564990), milliseconds on photos (1788213356119). Normalised it sits 1s to 7.4min before caption.created_at. A reel filmed weeks before it is posted would drag posted_at arbitrarily backwards, trading a late-date bug for an early-date bug. It is magnitude-normalised and used only when no publish candidate exists.
2. The brief's scenario 2 assumed the carousel has all three equal. It does not: DcteA8RFPVR has taken_at 1788192110 and caption.created_at 1788192113, caption 3s LATER. Earliest-of returns 1788192110, genuinely unchanged as the scenario requires; "prefer the caption when present" would have shifted a date that was already correct. Earliest is also the only rule safe in both directions - it corrects an inflated taken_at AND ignores a caption edited after the post.

postedAtSource keeps its exact existing union. DurablePostDiscoveryService branches on === 'provider' at :364, :374, :394 and persists the value to Item.postedAtSource and PostDiscoveryCandidate.timestampSource, so widening it would break those checks and write new values into existing columns. The winning candidate goes in a new in-memory postedAtField instead - satisfies "record the source" with zero consumer churn and no migration. Flagged to the supervisor that a durable column is a one-line additive change on request.

TWO BUGS FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING, BOTH FIXED
1. The discovery metadata top-up (posts.service.ts ~:1757) writes its resolved timestamp BACK into the item, and that item becomes Item.rawPayload. Left on the corrected resolver it would have written caption-derived values into raw_payload.taken_at, making the raw payload no longer raw and silently invalidating the exact comparison the drift report depends on. That call site now uses rawInstagramTakenAt; only the derived postedAt is corrected.

Production actually holds legacy=592, null=65, provider=33, and 'observed_fallback' does not occur at all - so that gate hid 657 of 690 rows, i.e. every historical row the operator needs. Surface A (Items Card View) — 14 findings, each traced to the producing line. All seven triage items confirmed against the code, and the two headline metrics are worse than the triage suggested: Surge Score is not merely unformatted (PostMetricsCard.vue:193-196 toString()) but on the wrong scale, because two Surge definitions ship — the ratio at item-snapshots.service.ts:546-547 and the product's canonical 0-100 z-score at pulse/surge.util.ts, which is what the comps and the creator dashboard show. Depth Rate is a ratio through toFixed(1) (PostMetricsCard.vue:202-205 over item-snapshots.service.ts:543-544), so it is mathematically stuck at 0.0 while the already-computed depth_score_pct sits unused. "Cooling" on every card is a threshold written for a 0-1 scale reading a ~0.001 value (item-snapshots.service.ts:558-576), fed by `shares ?? 0` where offered_fields already records that shares were never offered; that 4-label vocabulary is also not the product's canonical 3-arc one (pulse/snapshot-arc.util.ts). Caption-as-title is structural: postTitle is only set when title !== caption (index.vue:1604, :1837) and title is the caption via extractTitleFromCaption (index.vue:1527-1532), rendered 20px/600 white centred over the full 200px header with no clamp (PostMetricsCard.vue:15, :313-330). utils/postCardMetrics.ts is a fork of shared/metric-fallback.util.ts that drops 'not_offered', so the card cannot say what PostSnapshotsSection.vue:148 already says.

Three defects found beyond the triage list, two of them user-visible data errors:
(1) Engagement rate is under-reported 100x whenever it comes from a snapshot — the backend emits engagement_rate as a ratio (item-snapshots.service.ts:542) while the frontend import fallback emits a percent (postCardMetrics.ts:112-129), and both land in `${v.toFixed(1)}%`. Four more copies of that formatter exist in admin surfaces (PostSnapshotsSection.vue:843, ItemSnapshotsModal.vue:667, ContentInventoryTable.vue:303, AdminCampaignPostTable.vue:520), so this is likely not confined to the card.
(2) index.vue:1343-1344 takes snapshots[length-1] as "latest" with no ordering guarantee while currentSurgeScore/DepthRate/SnapshotLabel come from the true latest (item-snapshots.service.ts:578-591), so the three headline rows and six detail rows can describe different snapshots.
(3) Every in-card control also navigates: PostMetricsCard.vue:60,71,82,93,105 fire plain @click, and the .stop at index.vue:428-431 is on the CUSTOM events, which cannot stop native click bubbling to the wrapper's @click="viewItem". With the span unsized, CustomIcon.vue:187-194's width:100%!important falls back to the SVG's 300px default replaced size, height from the 18:20 viewBox. Same string-size bug at OnboardingLoadingStep.vue:9 and DocModal.vue:18; AdminSidebar.vue:8 uses :size="18" and renders correctly, which is the proof of the difference.
